astronomy_picture_of_the_day.title: Trifid Pillars and Jets
astronomy_picture_of_the_day.explanation: Dust pillars are like interstellar mountains.  They survive because they are more dense than their surroundings, but they are slowly being  eroded away by a hostile environment.  Visible in the featured picture by the Hubble Space Telescope is the end of a huge gas and dust pillar in the Trifid Nebula (M20), punctuated by a smaller pillar pointing up and an unusual jet pointing to the upper left. …
